title: You Have 100 Days Left. Here’s How to Reset Your Life
summary: Part one of a two-part 'back to school' series arguing that fall, not January, is the best time to reinvent yourself with roughly 100 days left in the year. The sisters preview five Q4 tips and go deep on tip one, revisiting January goals: Cherie reviews her 2026 bingo board and Jean her '37 things while 37' list, and both revise goals that had become overly prescriptive, ending with homework to spend 20 minutes reviewing your own goals without judgment.

ideas.idea: January is not the best time to reinvent yourself; the fall is, because back-to-school energy plus roughly 100 days left is the perfect window to recommit to goals.
ideas.detail: Even if you are no longer in school, the seasonal 'sharpen your pencils' energy is renewing, and Q3-to-Q4 is a natural check-in to reignite, re-tackle or let go of goals set in January and go out with a bang.

ideas.idea: Five back-to-school tips for Q4: revisit your January goals, reset your physical and mental space, recommit to a routine, book yourself a future gift, and set aside time to nurture yourself in a 'cocoon'.
ideas.detail: This episode covers tip one in depth; tips two through five are saved for part two of the series.

ideas.idea: Review personal goals quarterly the way businesses do, instead of waiting until year end.
ideas.detail: Pull out your journal, vision board or bingo board and ask: which goals have I accomplished, which have meaningful progress, which no longer feel important and can be deprioritized, and which were actually mine versus created from someone else's expectations.

ideas.idea: A 5x5 bingo card of goals spanning fun, health, travel and intellectual growth is a balanced, visual way to picture a full year.
ideas.detail: Cherie's 2026 card includes read 10 books (on book six), start a personal trainer (done), ski a new mountain, speak at a conference, attend a gala, host a live event, get a Korean body scrub, go to a concert and score sub-100 in golf; she leaves one square blank on purpose to fill later rather than rush something in.

ideas.idea: Attaching a number or streak to a restorative goal, like 'sauna 10 times' or 'journal 30 days in a row,' turns relaxation into work and should be revised.
ideas.detail: Cherie has done sauna once and swum zero of a planned five times; last year Jean strained her back attempting 'gym 30 days in a row.' The fix is to write just 'sauna' or 'journal 30 days total' as a reminder and track it loosely rather than as a pressured action item.

ideas.idea: Reviewing a goal board can reveal that you completed every activity that needed booking but none of the do-nothing goals you intentionally added to slow down.
ideas.detail: After a go-go-go, career-oriented 2025 card, Cherie built rest into 2026 (relax at a spa, get a massage, sit in a park 30 minutes with no phone) yet those are the only unfinished squares, so her last 100 days are about chilling out.

ideas.idea: It is fine to carry a goal over to next year if you still care about it, especially one that must be chipped away at rather than achieved overnight.
ideas.detail: Cherie's sub-100 golf goal carried over from 2025; she has been taking lessons and playing and may carry it to 2027.

ideas.idea: Ask whether each goal is intrinsic or came from an external obligation, and reframe it so it serves you.
ideas.detail: Cherie's 'travel internationally' was fulfilled by a wedding and a work trip, obligations she was happy to meet but not her own itinerary; her next goal is to travel internationally purely for fun.

ideas.idea: Write a long list of 'N things to do while N years old' plus a one-paragraph theme, and count it a win if you hit N of them.
ideas.detail: Jean's list for 37 runs to about 70 items across health, career, creativity/fun, personal self-investment, relationships, finances and things to look forward to by month. Her 2026 theme is 'investing in myself to create opportunities for magic beyond my wildest dreams.'

ideas.idea: Make sleep goals measurable with a wearable, e.g. raise sleep score from 74% to 80% and move average bedtime from 2:21am to 12:20am.
ideas.detail: Jean tracks with a Whoop; her average bedtime was literally 2:21am when she wrote the goal and is now much closer to 12:20am, though she hasn't hit the 80% score yet.

ideas.idea: Commitments to yourself must be calendared like a date with someone else, or work will always fill the time.
ideas.detail: Jean's goal to 'go on dates even if it's with myself' has been neglected; Cherie prescribes reserving Friday or Saturday night, roughly 7-10pm, religiously off from work.

ideas.idea: Some goals are simply too big and should be right-sized: 30-plus social events meeting new people is a lot, and a full split in 100 days may be injurious.
ideas.detail: Jean has made progress on socializing via Venice events but 30 'sounds like a lot'; the sisters ask listeners whether Jean can learn a full split without injury in the next 100 days.

ideas.idea: Homework: spend 20 minutes this week revisiting January goals without judging yourself, because the plan is written in pencil.
ideas.detail: Take inventory of what worked and what didn't, then revise; it is okay to have a plan, but you have the ability to change it to what works for the next 100 days.
